I would be careful about framing it as "financial partner OR operating partner." Based on everything you've told me, what you're actually asking for is a **true partnership**, where responsibilities are divided and owned. Right now you're carrying both your responsibilities and most of his.

I'd also address the phone call directly without using emotional language like "tantrum." If your goal is to be heard, it's stronger to describe the impact.

:::writing{variant="email" id="68492" subject="We Need Immediate Clarity on Roles, Responsibilities, and the Future of Luxora"}
Eric,

I have spent a lot of time reflecting over the last several weeks, and I need to have a very direct conversation about where we are as partners and where Luxora is headed.

First, I want you to know this email is not coming from a place of anger. It is coming from a place of exhaustion, concern, and a genuine desire to create a structure that allows both of us and the company to succeed.

The reality is that I am no longer functioning as a CEO.

I am currently functioning as the CEO, COO, Head of Sales, Lead Closer, Marketing Director, Content Creator, Copywriter, Funnel Strategist, Product Developer, Client Success Manager, Recruiter, Trainer, Operations Manager, Project Manager, and primary fulfillment person all at the same time.

Every day I am creating content, filming videos, building funnels, refining offers, running sales calls, handling client fulfillment, managing team members, onboarding contractors, solving technical problems, creating systems, developing products, recruiting setters and closers, hiring, training, managing vendors, and trying to keep the company moving forward.

That is not sustainable.

I am burning out.

The hardest part is not the workload itself. I have always been willing to work hard. The hardest part is carrying responsibility for virtually every operational function of the company while simultaneously feeling like the results of the company rest solely on my shoulders.

This morning was a perfect example.

I came to you looking for support, partnership, solutions, and help carrying the weight of what is happening inside the business.

Instead, I left that conversation feeling blamed for outcomes that are impossible for one person to control while simultaneously performing the jobs of an entire executive team.

That is not what I need from my business partner.

I need support.

I need collaboration.

I need ownership.

I need someone who believes in what we are building enough to help solve problems, not simply point them out.

After speaking with Gil's team and spending time evaluating everything that has happened over the past several months, I believe our biggest issue is not ads, marketing, setters, closers, or lead generation.

Our biggest issue is a lack of clarity around ownership, authority, accountability, and responsibilities.

We have built a situation where I am effectively operating the company while also trying to carry the responsibilities that should be divided between partners.

That is not a criticism.

It is simply the current reality.

If Luxora is going to grow, then we need to clearly define who owns what and hold each other accountable to those responsibilities.

From my perspective, this is what that structure looks like:

My Responsibilities:
• Vision and strategy
• Product development
• Sales leadership
• Client relationships
• Team leadership
• Marketing direction
• Growth initiatives
• Brand development
• Client fulfillment oversight
• Training systems
• Operational execution

Your Responsibilities:
• Financial oversight
• Budgeting
• Cash flow management
• Capital planning
• Banking relationships
• Expense management
• Financial reporting
• Strategic partnerships
• Business development
• Joint venture opportunities
• Vendor negotiations
• Industry relationships
• High-level hiring and firing decisions
• Organizational accountability
• Helping build the company's network and opportunities
• Investor and growth relationships
• Supporting leadership decisions once they are made

I do not believe your role should be limited to finances.

I believe your role should be helping expand Luxora through relationships, partnerships, opportunities, introductions, strategic deals, and helping us open doors that accelerate growth.

What I cannot continue doing is carrying operations, sales, marketing, fulfillment, recruiting, hiring, content creation, strategy, and business development simultaneously while also being expected to shoulder responsibility for every challenge the company faces.

No company scales that way.

No CEO succeeds long term that way.

And no partnership remains healthy that way.

I also need immediate access and visibility into every critical business account, financial system, operational platform, vendor relationship, and business asset. We cannot allow the company to be vulnerable because critical information or access is concentrated in one place.

Most importantly, I need clarity.

Not next month.

Not after Vegas.

Not after another round of discussions.

Now.

Because the company cannot continue operating in this gray area.

I care deeply about what we have built.

I believe in Luxora.

I believe in our clients.

I believe in our mission.

And I still believe in the possibility of us being great partners.

But that requires both of us clearly understanding our responsibilities, owning them, and supporting each other when things get difficult.

Right now, I need a partner.

Not another responsibility.

I need us to decide immediately what this partnership is going to look like moving forward so we can either build this company together with clarity or have the difficult conversations necessary to determine a different path.

Luxora deserves clarity.

Our team deserves clarity.

And honestly, both of us deserve clarity.

Bethany

Co-Founder & CEO
The Luxora Collective
:::

This version shifts the conversation from "Eric should step aside" to "Eric needs to step up into clearly defined partnership responsibilities," which sounds much closer to what you're actually asking for.

Yes. The current version reads like you're at a breaking point. If your goal is to get Eric to listen instead of defend himself, I'd soften the emotional language and make it more about **structure, growth, and clarity**.

For example, I'd change this:

> "I am burning out."

To:

> "I am reaching a point where the current structure is no longer sustainable if we want Luxora to grow the way we both envisioned."

I'd change this:

> "Instead, I left that conversation feeling blamed for outcomes that are impossible for one person to control..."

To:

> "I left that conversation feeling like we were focused on assigning responsibility rather than solving the underlying challenges together. What I was hoping for was a discussion around how we can better divide responsibilities and support each other moving forward."

I'd change this:

> "That is not what I need from my business partner. I need support. I need collaboration. I need ownership."

To:

> "What I need moving forward is greater clarity, collaboration, and shared ownership of the areas that will help Luxora grow."

I'd change this:

> "Right now, I need a partner. Not another responsibility."

To:

> "Right now, I believe we have an opportunity to become stronger partners by creating clearer ownership, accountability, and expectations for both of us."

And honestly, I'd replace this entire section:

> "No company scales that way.
>
> No CEO succeeds long term that way.
>
> And no partnership remains healthy that way."

With:

> "As Luxora grows, I believe we need to evolve the structure of the business so that responsibilities are aligned with each person's strengths and capacity. That is the only way we will create something scalable and sustainable."

Then I'd end with something like:

> "I am incredibly optimistic about what we are building. I do not believe we are behind. In fact, I believe we are closer than ever to creating something special. What I believe we need now is greater clarity around roles, ownership, and accountability so that both of us can focus on what we do best and move the company forward together."

That keeps the message strong, but it reads like a CEO presenting a solution rather than someone expressing frustration. It is much harder to argue with and much easier to say "yes" to.

This should be firm, honest, and solution-oriented. The goal is not to attack him. The goal is to force clarity and a decision.

:::writing{variant="email" id="58371" subject="We Need Immediate Clarity on Roles, Ownership, and the Future of Luxora"}
Eric,

I have spent a lot of time reflecting over the last several weeks, and I need to have a very direct conversation with you about where we are as partners and where Luxora is headed.

First, I want you to know that this email is not written from a place of anger. It is written from a place of exhaustion, concern, and a genuine desire to find a path forward that works for both of us.

The reality is that I am no longer operating as a CEO. I am currently functioning as the CEO, COO, Head of Sales, Lead Closer, Marketing Director, Content Creator, Copywriter, Funnel Strategist, Product Developer, Client Success Manager, Recruiter, Trainer, Operations Manager, Project Manager, and primary fulfillment person all at the same time.

Every day I am creating content, filming videos, building funnels, refining offers, running sales calls, handling client fulfillment, managing team members, onboarding contractors, solving technical problems, creating systems, developing products, recruiting setters and closers, and trying to keep the company moving forward.

That is not sustainable.

I am burning out.

The hardest part is not the workload itself. I have always been willing to work hard. The hardest part is carrying the responsibility for virtually every operational function in the company while simultaneously being held accountable for results that depend on areas where I do not have complete control.

When things go well, it feels like we are partners.

When things go wrong, it often feels like the responsibility shifts back onto me.

That is not a partnership structure that can continue long term.

After speaking with Gil and spending time evaluating everything that has happened over the past several months, I believe our biggest issue is not marketing, ads, setters, closers, or lead generation.

Our biggest issue is a lack of clarity around ownership, authority, accountability, and roles.

We have built a situation where I am effectively running the entire company while decisions, expectations, and accountability are still being shared in a way that does not reflect reality.

The reality is that I am operating the business.

The reality is that most day-to-day decisions, execution, strategy, client relationships, sales, marketing, fulfillment, and growth initiatives are currently being driven by me.

That is not a criticism. It is simply the current state of the business.

I need clarity on whether you want to be an operating partner or a financial partner.

If you want to be an operating partner, then I need meaningful ownership of operational responsibilities from you. That means consistent participation, execution, leadership, and accountability in specific areas of the business.

If you want to be a financial partner, then I believe we need to formally define that role and allow me to run operations without constant uncertainty around who owns what.

From my perspective, the most logical structure would be:

My Responsibilities:
• Vision and strategy
• Product development
• Sales leadership
• Client relationships
• Team leadership
• Partnerships
• Marketing direction
• Growth initiatives

Your Responsibilities:
• Financial oversight
• Budgeting
• Cash flow management
• Capital planning
• Banking relationships
• Expense management
• Financial reporting
• Investor-level strategic input

This would allow each of us to operate within our strengths instead of constantly overlapping in areas where confusion is slowing us down.

I also need immediate access and visibility into every critical business account, financial system, operational platform, and vendor relationship. We cannot put ourselves in a position again where the business is vulnerable because one person has exclusive access to something critical.

Most importantly, I need a decision.

Not next month.

Not after Vegas.

Not after another round of discussions.

Now.

Because the company cannot continue operating in this gray area.

I care deeply about what we have built.

I believe in Luxora.

I believe in the mission.

I believe in the clients we serve.

I believe in the future of this company.

But I cannot continue carrying the responsibilities of an entire executive team while simultaneously trying to navigate unclear authority, unclear expectations, and unclear ownership of responsibilities.

I need to know whether we are moving forward with a clearly defined structure where responsibilities, authority, and accountability are aligned, or whether we need to have a larger conversation about the future partnership itself.

I care about you and want what is best for both of us. That is why I am being honest.

I am asking for clarity, commitment, and a decision.

Because Luxora deserves it.

Bethany
Co-Founder & CEO
The Luxora Collective
:::

This version keeps the focus on business realities and role clarity rather than making it feel like a personal attack, which will give you the best chance of getting a productive response instead of a defensive one.

Yes. The P.S. is repeating a lot of what you've already said. I'd shorten it to something like this:

:::writing{variant="standard" id="31582"}
P.S. I spent some time thinking through what I believe a healthy organizational structure for Luxora would look like.

My role as CEO should primarily focus on vision, strategy, product development, sales leadership, partnerships, brand growth, and leading the team.

Your role should focus on financial oversight, budgeting, cash flow, hiring and firing decisions, accountability, business development, strategic partnerships, industry relationships, referral channels, joint ventures, and opening doors that create growth opportunities for the company.

Jacques should own marketing execution, including ads, landing pages, analytics, testing, optimization, and reporting.

Aanchal should own operational coordination, follow-up, reporting, onboarding, and keeping projects moving forward.

Setters should own outreach and appointment generation.

Closers should own sales conversations and revenue generation.

Lamonica's team should own organic content strategy, scheduling, reporting, and growth.

The biggest gap I currently see is business development. While I am focused on building Luxora internally, someone needs to be focused on building Luxora externally through partnerships, referral relationships, strategic alliances, networking, and growth opportunities.

Ultimately, my goal is not to remove anyone from the business. My goal is to clearly define ownership so that every person can operate in their strengths, be accountable for results, and help Luxora grow without one person carrying the weight of every department.
:::

This keeps the point but cuts it from nearly 1,000 words to about 250 and is much more likely to actually be read.

:::writing{variant="email" id="52841" subject="Creating Clarity for the Next Phase of Luxora"}
Eric,

I have spent a lot of time reflecting over the last several weeks, and I think it is important that we have a direct conversation about where we are as partners and where Luxora is headed.

First, I want you to know this email is not coming from a place of frustration or blame. It is coming from a place of wanting to create clarity, alignment, and a structure that allows both of us and the company to succeed.

As I have evaluated where we are today, I have realized that many of the challenges we are experiencing are not necessarily marketing problems, sales problems, or lead generation problems.

I believe our biggest challenge is a lack of clearly defined ownership, authority, accountability, and responsibilities.

Over the past several months, I have naturally stepped into a large number of roles inside the company. In addition to leading the vision and growth strategy, I have also been heavily involved in sales, content creation, recruiting, fulfillment, marketing direction, operations, client management, and product development.

While I am willing to do whatever is necessary to move the company forward, I do not believe this structure is sustainable if we want Luxora to grow into what we originally envisioned.

This morning's conversation helped reinforce that for me.

When I reached out, what I was really looking for was a discussion around how we can better divide responsibilities, create more ownership, and support each other moving forward. I believe that is where our focus needs to be.

After speaking with Gil's team and evaluating everything that has happened over the past several months, I believe we have a tremendous opportunity in front of us. We are not behind. We are not failing. We simply need more clarity around who owns what so that each of us can operate in our strengths.

From my perspective, my primary responsibilities should be:

• Vision and strategy  
• Product development  
• Sales leadership  
• Client relationships  
• Team leadership  
• Brand growth and positioning  
• Marketing direction  
• Operational leadership  

I also believe there is a significant opportunity for you to help drive Luxora's growth through:

• Financial oversight and planning  
• Budgeting and cash flow management  
• Strategic partnerships  
• Business development  
• Joint ventures  
• Industry relationships  
• Referral partnerships  
• Vendor negotiations  
• High-level hiring and firing decisions  
• Organizational accountability  
• Opening doors and creating opportunities for the company  

I do not see your role as simply managing finances.

I see your role as helping expand Luxora externally while I focus on building Luxora internally.

As we continue to grow, I also believe it is important that we create visibility and access across all critical business systems, accounts, vendors, and financial platforms so that the company is protected and can operate smoothly regardless of circumstances.

Most importantly, I think we need to make some decisions and create clear ownership moving forward.

Not because anything is broken.
